# Goban Studio v2.0.0

A new Goban Studio: one board, three places — **Play**, **Practice**,
**Library** — and KataGo behind all of it.

## Download and first launch

| Platform | File | First launch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| macOS (Apple Silicon) | `GobanStudio-macOS-arm64.dmg` or `.zip` | Ad-hoc signed, **not notarized**. Right-click the app → Open once. If macOS still blocks it: `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/Goban\ Studio.app` |
| Windows (x64) | `GobanStudio-Windows-x64.zip` | **Not Authenticode-signed.** If SmartScreen appears, choose More info → Run anyway. WebView2 is preinstalled on Windows 10/11. |

`SHA256SUMS` lists the checksums of all three files.

## What's new

**A first run that fits you.** Pick a language, then say whether you have
never played, know the rules, or play regularly. You land in lesson one, a
gentle 9×9 game, or a 19×19 game at your level.

**KataGo everywhere.** Every board size now plays against KataGo, at a
strength from about 30 kyu to about 2 dan. Weaker levels choose among the
moves KataGo considered within a loss window for that rank, so the opponent
makes human-sized mistakes instead of random ones. Handicap is suggested
from your level.

**Review that explains.** Any game — current, saved, imported or classic —
opens in review. KataGo analyses every position, draws the balance of the
game and picks the three moves that lost the most. For each one you can
play through what happened and KataGo's better line on the board.

**Counting without the chores.** After two passes KataGo marks the dead
stones; the score counts up and you accept it or keep playing.

**A real course.** Eight units of short, multi-step lessons — from placing
the first stone to capturing races and counting — with explanations,
placement exercises and live problems.

**Problems that answer back.** Every problem is played against a built-in
solver: a wrong move is met with the actual refutation, a right move with
the most stubborn defence. Problems are grouped by topic, graded by measured
difficulty, and come back on a spaced-review schedule in the daily five.

**A library you curate.** Finished and saved games only, with thumbnails,
filters and search; the game in progress is a single Continue card. Classic
games and forty pro openings live here too, as guess-the-move studies.

**Quieter, clearer interface.** A new type scale (nothing under 12 px), light
and dark appearance that follows the system, wood/paper/slate boards,
coordinates outside the grid, stones that settle and captures that fade,
a focus mode, full keyboard control including playing on the board, and
screen-reader announcements for moves.

## Changed or removed

- The v1 “300 tsumego” were 25 one-move shapes repeated by rotation and
  translation, with difficulty labels assigned in rotation. They are gone.
  Every v2 problem is proved by the solver in the test suite, and its grade
  is measured, not assigned.
- The v1 “60 lessons” were single clicks; v2 replaces them with the course.
- Review is now part of every game instead of a separate tab; Settings opens
  as a sheet (⌘, / Ctrl+,).
- Pass now asks for confirmation; shortcuts use ⌘/Ctrl instead of bare
  letters.
- Abandoned games no longer fill the library.

## Your data

Settings, opening and classic progress, your streak, the game in progress
and every saved game carry over from v1 automatically. Progress on the
removed v1 drills and lessons does not carry over.

## Under the hood

- The KataGo sidecar gains an analysis command (`kata-search_analyze`, with
  a `kata-genmove_analyze` fallback) behind a new `studio.katagoAnalyze`
  bridge call; positions with handicap or SGF setup stones are now sent to
  KataGo too.
- The release self-test now requires KataGo analysis on 9×9 and 19×19 and a
  legal move in a handicap game from the packaged app.
- The interface is rebuilt on Preact (MIT, bundled; no network).
